briefings.headline: Make Pallante work; hunt the fastball
briefings.message: Andre Pallante is the high-confidence starter prediction; Matthew Liberatore is the alternative. Bryan Reynolds, Oneil Cruz, and Rafael Flores Jr. have reported batter edges. Be ready for fastballs—Pallante uses them 55.6% of the time to lefties—but don’t chase his slider, which has a 31.0% whiff rate. Flores Jr.’s breaking-ball results are a small sample; stay selective there. Their bullpen to watch includes Riley O'Brien, Ryne Stanek, George Soriano, and left-hander Justin Bruihl.
reminders: Hunt a fastball you can drive; stay disciplined against breaking balls.
Make Pallante earn the strike zone—don’t expand for the slider.
Be ready for rested late-inning relievers, including left-hander Justin Bruihl.

briefings.headline: Vary locations against their left-handed threats
briefings.message: Jared Jones starts with an 85-pitch limit and a target of 5.0 innings. Attack early, then use the slider as a chase pitch while varying locations. Jordan Walker can be vulnerable to breaking balls when ahead, but locate carefully; don’t give Alec Burleson predictable fastballs. Leo Bernal’s pitch splits are small-sample evidence, so don’t assume breaking balls are a weakness. Use rested high-leverage arms in close late innings, and consider left-handed relief for Burleson or Bernal when the matchup fits.
reminders: Keep Jones’s pitch mix varied; use the slider to Walker when ahead.
Avoid predictable fastballs to Burleson; vary location carefully to Bernal.
Use the bullpen by leverage; Gregory Soto is the primary closer.
